title: Polynomial finite-free model of the infinitesimal derived limit
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], and the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Separated, finite type and proper morphisms use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally finitely presented on etale scheme charts. Use quasi-coherent modules on the small etale ringed sites [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and tensor pullback and direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. A module is finitely presented if etale locally it has a presentation $\mathcal O^r\to\mathcal O^s\to F\to0$ with $r,s$ finite. Base-flatness means flatness of stalks on etale scheme charts over the corresponding local rings of the base [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Proper support means there exist a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ with $Z$ proper over the base and a finite type quasi-coherent module $G$ on $Z$ such that $i_*G\simeq F$ [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. Let $(A_n)_{n\geq1}$ be an inverse sequence of commutative rings with surjective transition maps whose kernels are locally nilpotent, meaning every element of each kernel is nilpotent, and set $A=\varprojlim_n A_n$. Let $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be separated and finitely presented, put $X_n=X\times_A\operatorname{Spec}A_n$. For every $n\geq1$ let $M_n$ be a finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-module, flat over $A_n$, with support proper over $A_n$, with specified isomorphisms $M_n\otimes_{A_n}A_{n-1}\simeq M_{n-1}$ for $n\geq2$. Use unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ for the full subcategory with quasi-coherent cohomology. Regard $M_n$ as a module on $X$ by direct image along $X_n\hookrightarrow X$; the given transition isomorphisms followed by quotient maps define its inverse-system maps. The symbol $R\varprojlim_{D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}}M_n$ denotes the homotopy inverse limit in this full derived subcategory: it fits into the product triangle $K\to\prod_{n\geq1}M_n\xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}}\prod_{n\geq1}M_n\to K[1]$, with products taken in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ and projections $q_n:K\to M_n$ induced by the first arrow. Here the shift has $n$th component equal to the transition map composed with the $(n+1)$st projection. Let $K$ be this homotopy inverse limit [lem-sfb-space-inverse-module-derived-limit]. Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\to X$ be an affine etale scheme chart, and let $P=A[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\twoheadrightarrow B$ be a surjective $A$-algebra map with $r$ finite [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. There exists a bounded-above complex $E^\bullet$ of finite free $P$-modules representing $R\Gamma(U,K)$ after restriction of scalars to $P$. For every $f\in P$, with image $\bar f\in B$, the localized complex $E^\bullet_f$ represents $R\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B_{\bar f},K)$ after restriction of scalars to $P_f$. Both representations respect the action of $A$. These complexes are K-flat over $A$: tensoring them termwise with any acyclic complex of $A$-modules gives an acyclic total tensor complex. In particular $E^\bullet_f\otimes_A R$ represents $R\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B_{\bar f},K)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}R$ for every $A$-algebra $R$, including $f=1$.

The localized K-flat finite-free model is the one used in 0CX9.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-inverse-module-derived-limit], $K$ has quasi-coherent cohomology and is bounded above. The affine base is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so [lem-sfb-space-fp-qcqs-source] makes $X$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For each perfect $E$, [lem-sfb-space-inverse-module-perfect-tests] gives a bounded finite-projective representative of $R\Gamma(X,K\otimes^{\mathbf L}E)$. Apply [lem-pc-finite-projective-complex-free-model] to this representative; its bounded-above finite-free replacement makes the tensor test pseudo-coherent by [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. The symmetry interchanging $K$ and $E$ identifies the tensor order with the following test criterion.

source.place: Tag 0CX7, lemma-relative-pseudo-coherence, first sentence, using 0CX5 and 0CX6

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-perfect-to-pseudocoherent-tests] with the upper bound and quasi-compact quasi-separated source just obtained. Thus $R\Gamma(X,E\otimes^{\mathbf L}K)$ is pseudo-coherent over $A$ for every pseudo-coherent $E$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-pseudocoherent-tests-relative]: its hypotheses are exactly separatedness and finite presentation of $X/A$, with no flatness of $X/A$ required. It follows that $K$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $A$.

source.place: Tag 0CX7, proof, using spaces-perfect.tex Tag 0CWH and spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 0CTT

proof.text: For every integer $m$, the all-etale-charts meaning in [lem-sfb-space-relative-pseudocoherence-etale-locality] gives relative $m$-pseudo-coherence of the scheme object $K_U$ corresponding to $K|_U$; hence $K_U$ is relatively pseudo-coherent. Use [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence] for this object and its pullbacks. Set $i:U\hookrightarrow V=\operatorname{Spec}P$ using the given surjection. The polynomial projection $V\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is flat by [lem-nagata-polynomial-projection-flat] and finitely presented (the finite set of generators $T_1,\ldots,T_r$ has no relations). Therefore [lem-sfb-flat-ambient-relative-pseudocoherence] gives pseudo-coherence of $Ri_*K_U$ on $V$.

source.place: Tag 0CX9, lemma-finitely-presented, polynomial-chart paragraph; more-morphisms.tex Tag 09UU

proof.text: Use [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] to represent the scheme object $K_U$ by $\widetilde{C^\bullet}$, where $Q(C^\bullet)=R\Gamma(U,K)$. On a standard open $D(f)\subset\operatorname{Spec}P$, the sections of $i_*\widetilde{C^j}$ are $C^j_{\bar f}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], which equal $(\operatorname{Res}_P C^j)_f$ by $c/\bar f^a\mapsto c/f^a$; these identifications commute with restrictions and differentials. Thus termwise $i_*\widetilde{C^\bullet}=\widetilde{\operatorname{Res}_P C^\bullet}$. For a K-injective resolution of $\widetilde{C^\bullet}$, [lem-pc-affine-pushforward-resolution-quasi-iso] says that its termwise pushforward still represents $Ri_*K_U$. Consequently this is the affine sheaf object of $\operatorname{Res}_P R\Gamma(U,K)$. Apply [lem-pc-affine-pseudo-coherent-criterion] to its pseudo-coherence from step 3 to obtain the asserted bounded-above finite-free complex $E^\bullet$. Its comparison in $D(P)$ respects $A\to P$.

For $f\in P$, localization is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], so it sends the isomorphism $Q(E^\bullet)\simeq C$ to an isomorphism $Q(E^\bullet_f)\simeq C\otimes_P P_f$. The affine derived pullback formula [lem-pc-affine-derived-pullback-tensor-tilde], followed by the quasi-inverse in [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence], identifies the latter with $R\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B_{\bar f},K)$ after restriction to $P_f$: on a $B$-module the fraction $c/f^j$ maps to $c/\bar f^j$, and $B\otimes_P P_f=B_{\bar f}$. Exactness allows this fraction identification on any representative of $C$. The etale comparison in step 3 commutes with this pullback. These maps preserve $A$ since $a(c/f^j)=(ac)/f^j$.

As an $A$-module each term $E^i\simeq P^{d_i}$ is free, with basis a finite union of the monomials in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Tensoring with such a module is a direct sum of copies of the input exact sequence, hence preserves exactness. Thus the terms are $A$-flat. Applying [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-localization-preserves-flatness] with $R=A$, algebra $P$, and the powers of $f$ shows that each $E^i_f$ is also $A$-flat. Localization preserves the upper bound and makes the terms finite free over $P_f$. Now [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] applied over $A$ to $E^\bullet$ and $E^\bullet_f$ gives precisely the asserted acyclic-total-tensor criterion. Finally apply [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] on the one-object ringed site to $A\to R$: these K-flat representatives compute the derived scalar extensions termwise for every $A$-algebra $R$. This includes $f=1$, $f=0$, $r=0$, and zero complexes.
